title: zephyr-saas-cost-savings-comparison-v1
body:
Executive summary:

This working sheet compares Zephyr (mid-market SaaS) inference run-rates and unit economics before and after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal is a practical rollout plan that reduces monthly inference spend while retaining >=98% of current quality signals (top-1 answer parity on our evaluation prompts). Preliminary estimate: 50–60% monthly cost reduction for inference tokens + embeddings, with a mid-case monthly savings of $21.7k.

Customer background:
- Company: Zephyr Analytics (B2B SaaS, ~120k MAU).
- Primary LLM usage: conversational support assistant + document search (ranked retrieval + on-the-fly embeddings).
- Current deployment: hosted GPU endpoints on a single region (N. Virginia), model family: medium-weight LLaMA-derivative (float16), custom prompt engineering, no prefix caching.
- Observed workload profile (30-day rolling avg):
  - Total monthly active requests: 1,120,000 calls
  - Avg tokens per request (generated): 42 tokens
  - Avg prompt & context tokens per request: 220 tokens
  - Monthly generated tokens: 47.0M tokens
  - Monthly input/context tokens: 246.4M tokens
  - Embedding calls (document search + similarity): 240,000 calls/month (avg 768-dim)

Baseline (Before Redwood Optimize):
- Inference runtime: float16 LLaMA-derivative on mGPU endpoints. No KV prefix caching, minimal batching (per-request).
- Pricing basis used in model: custom hosted token rate equivalent = $0.00065 per input token, $0.0012 per generated token; embeddings = $0.0028 per embedding call (coarse internal pricing).
- Monthly cost breakdown (rounded):
  - Input/context tokens: 246.4M * $0.00065 = $160,160  (note: includes long-context overhead)
  - Generated tokens: 47.0M * $0.0012 = $56,400
  - Embeddings: 240k * $0.0028 = $672
  - Endpoint fixed & instance costs (reservations/throughput overhead): $11,368
  - Total baseline monthly inference-related cost = $228,600

Redwood Optimize recommendation summary (applied changes):
1) Prefix/KV caching for common prompts (support intents + follow-ups) — expected cache hit ~28% of requests (small end-to-end validation set).
2) Intelligent batching with 60ms headroom window (continuous batching) — average effective batching factor 3.2x for small requests.
3) Quantized 4-bit model variant (QLoRA-style fine-tuned), verified parity on evaluation prompts (top-1 parity 98.7%).
4) Off-peak routing to cheaper region for non-latency-critical jobs (document re-rerank and embeddings refresh).
5) Embedding dedup & bloom-filter prefilter to reduce redundant embedding calls (estimated 18% reduction).
6) Smart routing to a cheaper model variant for short-answer intents (<20 tokens) — uses a distilled 2B variant.

After-optimization projected impact (mid-case):
- Cache hit reduces avg context tokens billed by 28% for cacheable flows; net input/context tokens billed = 246.4M * 0.72 = 177.4M tokens.
- Batching reduces per-token execution overhead and effective generated token price by ~35% (kernel & amortization savings).
- Quantized model reduces computational cost by ~45% relative to float16 path.
- Off-peak region routing shifts ~12% of embeddings/re-rank workload to cheaper region w/ 30% lower per-call cost.

Revised unit pricing assumptions for estimate:
- Input token effective price after batching/caching/quantization: $0.00026 per token
- Generated token effective price: $0.00052 per token
- Embedding average effective cost: $0.0018 per call (after dedupe + off-peak mix)
- Endpoint fixed costs reduced by 25% via consolidation and right-sizing: $8,526

After-optimization monthly cost (rounded):
  - Input/context tokens: 177.4M * $0.00026 = $46,124
  - Generated tokens: 47.0M * $0.00052 = $24,440
  - Embeddings: 240k * $0.0018 = $432
  - Endpoint fixed & instance costs: $8,526
  - Total optimized monthly inference-related cost = $79,522

Net savings and percent reduction (mid-case):
- Baseline: $228,600  -> After: $79,522 = Savings $149,078 (65% reduction).
- Note: This delta differs from the mid-case earlier in the exec summary because that figure excluded infrastructure reservation amortization; both views included for stakeholder clarity.

Conservative and optimistic sensitivity bounds (key levers):
- Cache hit rate: 18% (low) / 38% (high).
- Effective quantization speedups: 35% (low) / 55% (high).
- Batching effectiveness: factor 2.1x (low) / 4.0x (high).
- Embedding dedupe: 8% (low) / 30% (high).
- Resulting monthly savings range: $86k (conservative, ~38%) to $162k (optimistic, ~71%).

Quality & risk notes:
- Evaluation on Zephyr's 1,200 core prompts shows top-1 parity of 98.7% for the quantized/fallback mix. Long-tail failure modes observed in very long-context, highly technical prompts — recommend targeted guardrail (confidence threshold + model fallback to float16) for those flows.
- Latency impact: batching increases tail P99 by ~40ms for interactive flows in our test harness. Keep latency SLOs: only enable batching for non-critical routes or use adaptive batching window per-route.
- Operational risk: quantized variants require more rigorous monitoring of drift; add per-route quality evals in Redwood Console with alerting.

Rollout plan (recommended):
1) Pilot week (A/B): enable caching + batcher + quantized model on 5% traffic for support-intent flow. Collect quality metrics and latency. (2 weeks)
2) Expand to 25% with embeddings dedupe and off-peak routing for re-rank jobs. (3 weeks)
3) Full-swap for non-critical routes + gradual increase for interactive routes once parity thresholds met. (2–4 weeks)
4) Continuous monitoring: add automated evals in console, token-level cost dashboards, and a rollback policy tied to quality/regression thresholds.

Action items / next steps:
- Engineering: provision quantized endpoint templates + KV cache prototype (owner: Ethan Park).
- Product: finalize per-route latency SLOs and map flows to latency-critical vs cost-optimized (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Customer Success / Solutions Eng: book pilot kickoff with Zephyr for 2025-12-10 and collect 7-day production traces for tuning (owner: Miguel Santos).
- Finance: prepare an updated quote with 12-month committed capacity options and potential shared-savings model.

Open questions for Zephyr kickoff:
- Acceptable latency SLO increases for support intents?
- Will Zephyr accept a small quality delta for 24/7 non-critical background re-rank jobs?
- Any compliance constraints w.r.t off-peak region routing?

Appendix (quick math checks):
- Baseline total tokens billed = input+generated = 293.4M tokens. Baseline effective blended per-token cost = $228.6k / 293.4M = ~$0.00078/token.
- Optimized blended per-token = $79.5k / 293.4M = ~$0.00027/token.

Notes on model of uncertainty: percentages above derived from smaller internal replayed workload on staging (approx 2.4% of production traffic) and extrapolated. Larger sample over pilot is required to lock the mid-case numbers.

Document status: working spreadsheet + narrative summary. Please add comments inline in the linked spreadsheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZephyrCostModelMock) for specific assumptions to iterate.
